page.layout: One page of text, full width; a decorative border band across the middle; below it a centred Psalm reference and a motto in italic and black letter; then a note block of Latin lines in italic and a centred FINIS. No marginal notes; the right edge is cut off by the scan.

main_text.p: Quò ut nos omnes, decurso miserrimæ huius vitæ fastidioso curriculo, perducamur, faxit Rex illé regum, & Dominus dominantium: Cui soli honor & gloria in omnem æternitatem. Amen.
main_text.head: PSALM. CXIX. V. 96.

p.i: Omnis perfectionis (id est, rerum perfectarum & creaturarum) vidi finem, sed latum mandatum tuum est valde.
p.bl: Ich hab alles dings ein end gesehen, Aber o HERR dein gebott währet.

main_text.p: Oppidum pulcerrimum quodnam sit, & bellissimè munitum, ex Plauti descriptione:

p.i: Si incola bene sint morati, pulcrè munitum arbitror. Perfidi & peculatus ex urbe, & avaritia si exsulant. Quarta invidia: Quinta ambitio: Sexta obtrectatio: Septima perjurium: Octava indiligentia. Nona injuria: Decumum quod pessimum aggressu scelus. Hæc nisi aberunt centuplex murus rebus servandis parum est.

page.notes: Right edge of the text is cut off by the scan, so line ends are missing words (e.g. "huius", "faxit Rex", "Amen", "Perfi..."). Black letter German line and the decorative band are reproduced as far as legible. Some words in the Latin italic passage are uncertain and may be misread.
